name: Port Vila Centre
tagline: The seafront, the market house and the shops
description: The strip along Lini Highway facing the harbour, with the market house, the banks, most of the restaurants and the duty-free shops that serve the cruise ships. Everything administrative in Vanuatu happens within a few hundred metres of here.
bestFor: Short stays and anyone dealing with banks or immigration
pros: Market house for cheap fresh produce
Best restaurant cluster in the country
cons: Busy and loud on cruise ship days
Hot and short on shade at midday

name: Nambatu and Nambatri
tagline: The practical residential districts behind the centre
description: The neighbourhoods running inland and south from the centre, holding much of the town's ordinary housing, supermarkets and small businesses. They are where most residents actually live rather than where visitors stay, and rents are considerably below the waterfront.
bestFor: Longer stays at local rather than expatriate prices
pros: Rents well below the waterfront areas
cons: Nothing scenic about the area itself
Little to do in the evening

name: Tassiriki and Erakor Lagoon
tagline: Lagoon-side living a few minutes from town
description: The area around the Erakor lagoon south of the centre, with resorts, expatriate houses and a small ferry across to Erakor Island. The water is calm and swimmable, the setting is green, and it is the most pleasant place to be based within reach of town.
bestFor: Anyone wanting water at the door without resort pricing everywhere
pros: Calm lagoon water for swimming and paddling
Green and quiet but close to the centre
Erakor Island ferry for a day out
cons: Mosquitoes near the lagoon at dusk
Needs a vehicle or regular taxis

name: Pango
tagline: The peninsula village south of town
description: A village on the peninsula southwest of Port Vila, with a mix of ni-Vanuatu households and expatriate houses on the ridge, a good surf break at Pango Point and views back across the bay. It is ten minutes from the centre and feels considerably further.
bestFor: Quiet stays with a surf break and a view
pros: Surf break and coastline at the door
Quiet village setting close to town
cons: Almost no shops or services locally

name: Mele
tagline: The large village west, near the cascades
description: One of the largest villages in Vanuatu, on the coast northwest of town near the Mele Cascades and the beach that shares its name. It is rural, cheap and entirely ni-Vanuatu, about fifteen minutes from the centre along the ring road.
bestFor: Budget stays and anyone wanting village rather than town life
pros: Much cheaper than anywhere near the centre
Mele Cascades and the beach nearby
cons: Fifteen minutes from town with limited transport
Internet weaker than in the centre
Very few services aimed at outsiders
